Created: 2026-05-17 10:06 PDT
Updated: 2026-05-17 10:06 PDT

Related: [[N24 RaceWatch]]

## Summary

RaceWatch concurrent websocket load watcher for `https://n24racewatch.com/api/n24-racewatch/realtime/health`.

- Watch window: 2026-05-16 16:05:50 PDT to 2026-05-17 08:47:40 PDT.
- Duration: 16h 41m 50s.
- Samples: 282.
- Cadence: roughly 60 seconds from 16:05 to 17:46 PDT, then 5 minutes from 17:47 PDT onward.
- Metric: `clients` from the realtime health endpoint, which counts open realtime websocket connections, not unique humans.
- High point: 60 connected websocket clients at 2026-05-17 03:07:30 PDT.
- Low point: 14 connected websocket clients at 2026-05-16 16:33:55 PDT.
- Time-weighted average: 39.5 connected websocket clients.
- Simple sample average: 35.0 connected websocket clients. The time-weighted average is the better headline because the first low-load segment was sampled much more frequently.
- Preflight check before the watcher started returned 24 clients at about 2026-05-16 16:05:34 PDT; this was excluded from the averages.

## Shape

The curve started in the high teens/low 20s, climbed through the 30s by early evening, settled into the low/mid 40s from about 20:00 to midnight, then built into the overnight peak. The strongest sustained period was roughly 01:00-03:15 PDT, mostly low/mid 50s, topping at 60. After 03:15 it stepped down into the mid/high 40s, briefly recovered around 05:00, then faded steadily through the morning to the mid 20s by the final sample.

All visible watcher readings reported upstream state `connected`. The endpoint `generatedAt` field occasionally stalled while the `clients` value continued changing, so this note treats `clients` as the load signal and does not use `generatedAt` for freshness of each viewer count.
